reviews.title: Not for Neuro Divergents
reviews.text: Everything is based on speed. Not your ability to reason through complex problems. If you’re ND, this just makes you feel stupid, even tho you score 98 on nation wide tests. Speed doesn’t help NDs, it only frustrates them.

reviews.title: Great App for your brain
reviews.text: I don’t play these games enough, but every time I do several different exercises a few days in a row, I can actually tell that my memory, focus, and brain speed feel sharper. One reviewer said it’s frustrating, and yes any game you play can be, but even if I don’t get them all right and get frustrated, if I just stick with them and repeat the exercises, I find I get better, little by little. A lot of these exercises are really fun and I do the fun ones first, and the more challenging ones later. I know it’s working my brain and making new connections up in that mess of synapses. I’m 71 with ADD, in great physical shape, but as I age, I want my brain to be sharp and focused too. That’s so important. You gotta stick with it, don’t get upset about it, make it into a fun game that’s helping your brain in so many ways … it’ll pay off in the long run.

reviews.title: Fine Tuning
reviews.text: The games are worthwhile except for Fine Tuning where GA and DA sound exactly alike on my speakers and even when I wear earbuds.  Very rarely do I hear a clear DA. I usually earn only one star at a time making this exercise excruciating.  Do others actually hear a difference?

reviews.title: Should be better
reviews.text: Nice app with solid content and harder levels as you improve. You have to pay more money to access your own data and how exactly you are improving. All the app gives you are silly stars and meaningless pictures when you pass a game or level.  Who know where they sell your results.

reviews.title: to short free mode
reviews.text: i’d never pay for something like this when i can only see so little of how it works. prove you aren’t snake oil if you want a dime lol.

reviews.title: No phone available, unable to talk with anyone
reviews.text: I am highly frustrated by the inadequate service provided by this app. You are forced to pay for a subscription immediately before you can even properly test or play other games to evaluate the product. Worse yet, when you run into issues, there is no clearly visible or accessible customer support system to communicate with. The user experience feels locked behind a paywall without any safety net for troubleshooting. I am leaving this critical comment in the sincere hope that the management team and developers read this and change their restrictive model and hidden support structure.

reviews.title: Steaks your money
reviews.text: Once you’ve signed up you can never cancel the subscription!

reviews.title: multiple glitches
reviews.text: I have an iphone and one of the exercises (Divided Attention)does not recognize when I correctly tap the screen. I have brought this to their attention and they acknowledged the problem but have not fixed it. Another exercise (Hear,Hear) cuts off the sound that one is supposed to match- making it impossible to do so. Very frustrating. Maybe better off taking piano lessons than using this.

reviews.title: Yuck
reviews.text: Developing peer reviewed work into games that can help blunt public health impacts of dementia is great. Charging exorbitant subscription rates for it is evil. The science is funded, the game development is not terribly expensive, and using the studies as branding for the sake of profiteering is disgusting. Ordinary everyday capitalist evil, but evil. Non-jerks have tried to replicate UFOV games for free as open source options but of course they don’t have access to the progression algorithm data derived from the study which was monetized by the jerks.

reviews.title: Mediocre app but decent tool overall
reviews.text:
The app is a good exercise. One must recognize a few exercises have terrible instructions but most are adequate. The app is buggy in that it fails to always register your responses correctly leading tostrikes against you. That will piss you off.  Using AI to explore the clinical trials one does not find a validation  regarding the exercises efficacy, but after using it one does feel sharper while driving for example.

 Is it worth it?    Yes, I think,  once one knows the peculiarities. You may end up using the website rather than the app as I have. Support is mediocre. BrainHQ may also delete your review here.

reviews.title: Too fast
reviews.text: The feedback after completing exercises goes way too fast for me to read and you can’t go back to it anywhere. Please fix this!

reviews.title: I understand now
reviews.text:
A few days ago I wrote whining about how there was no way to progress part a point in the memory test with sound cards. 
I understand now.
Thanks

reviews.title: Visual Sweeps
reviews.text: The instructions for the visual sweeps exercise make absolutely no sense whatsoever.  It’s utterly impossible to do it.

reviews.title: okay but..
reviews.text: I’ve tried to like this but at a certain point in the daily training it starts going too way to fast- is it realistically made for humans? I have to literally position my fingers millimeters from screen in order to hit it fast enough? then it becomes just stress. it’s no on this one

reviews.title: Over charged
reviews.text: I purchased a 1 year subscription for $99.99 in March 2026 and I’ve been over charged. Once in April 26’ for 94.99 and twice in May. I want a refund!!! Unfair

reviews.title: Nice App
reviews.text: Works well on my iPhone 12 but I downloaded it on my mom’s Google Pixel (2025) and the navigation task bar (the info, pause and exit buttons) when playing games is completely gone, so she can’t exit or pause any games

reviews.title: Brilliant… but there is a huge accessibility problem.
reviews.text:
The tests are great. The system works very well, encouraging you to keep trying until you figure it out.

However.

There is no option for accessibility. Not even in the audio practice, which requires working ears.

I wrote support and asked, and they told me directly that they have no plans to address this. The brains of those with disabilities apparently are a very low priority.

I’m hoping it gets fixed eventually. This really is the best brain training game… but I don’t want to give my money to a company that views some humans as worth less effort.

reviews.title: Great, but….
reviews.text: I’m only using the daily free version.  Challenging, but fun!  My only quibble is that the card memory game doesn’t give enough time to respond!  Even hovering  fingers over the thumbs up and down buttons doesn’t allow enough time to tap

reviews.title: Erratic performance
reviews.text:
The sounds only work about 60% of the time, and they’re sporadic. Sound Sweep, for example, plays two tones for each challenge, and sometimes only the first one is audible, sometimes only the second one, sometimes both, and sometimes neither one. It beck
Ea. Guessing game, which is not helpful.  There are other challenges that exhibit erratic performance as well.

There are also some games - Card Shark being one example - that have very confusing and unclear instructions on how to play.

So far, this app is not proving very useful or worth the money for the paid version, although it IS helping me learn how to deal with frustration!

The similar app Impulse has proven better and more reliable.

reviews.title: Poor sound quality affects training
reviews.text: i’ve been doing one free daily training round, and enjoyed the first few, but then I got to treating where I have to listen to a conversation and answer questions about what was said. The problem that the sound quality of the app is so bad, I cannot understand that people are saying. My hearing is excellent, it’s not that. And the names that are chosen, are unusually spelled or uncommon, and that compounds the problem. I’m pretty disappointed with that

reviews.title: can’t get past start
reviews.text: I wish that every game presented had a clear demo or tutorial. I have little experience with video games and find myself completely puzzled at times, lost in terms of how to proceed. I’ve quit many tasks without making it past the “start” button, which is incredibly demoralizing. Is there a point to not providing more explanation?

reviews.title: No allowance for colorblindness
reviews.text: This app seems to be very good and helpful until you get to a spot where you’re depending on color and shades of color which it does a lot. I have sent messages and they  tell me to adjust my phone, so ,they make no allowances. My phones colorblind options don’t seem to be helpful. unfortunately there are many visual and optic challenges.on this app

reviews.title: Too repetitive, not enough feedback
reviews.text: I wish it provided more feedback on whether I was getting any better at the games. What feedback it does give flashes up so quickly, I can’t read it. I’m also getting a bit bored as there’s  only a handful of different games.

reviews.title: Unpolished
reviews.text:
OK, but it needs work. For example, the voice in the to-do list exercise is extremely unnatural and hard to understand. In that same exercise, the instructions are sometimes ambiguous; it’ll say something like “You need item A after item B and then item C.” That could mean either B, A, C, or B, C, A. Of the exercises I’ve tried so far, that one is the worst, but others could use some polishing too. There’s one (I can’t remember the name) where there’s an image with blurry lines that either converge or diverge. The speed advances so quickly to such a rate that it’s just a wild guess. I understand that it needs to get more difficult, but it goes from easy to impossible almost immediately.

I really want to like this app enough to subscribe, but the one-per-day free exercises I’ve seen so far are not encouraging.

UPDATE: the ambiguity in the to-do list exercise instructions is fixed, but the voice quality is still comically bad.

reviews.title: Sound not always clear
reviews.text: When playing one of the tests, I was unable to understand some of the names mentioned in the dialog which made it difficult to track the conversation. But worst was a game where we listened to a list of items to identify but the recording was broken up which made it difficult to follow.

reviews.title: App is great
reviews.text: Exercises are great. Give it a try. However, there was a glitch and had to reset subscription. Did not like that it just happened. App is working fine now and recommend to all to give it a try.

reviews.title: Gratuitous graphics give me headaches
reviews.text: The graphics go by so quickly and flash so much it hurts my head. I would love to find a list where it will tell me what I'm good at and what I'm struggling with.

reviews.title: Cannot manage through the app store
reviews.text:
I tried to purchase the app based on their directions. However, they no longer allow app purchases through Apple. You have to purchase through their website so they don't have to pay Apple the $30.00 app fee. I don't want a web-bases app. Without it you get one free game per day. 

I instead purchased another app at half the price. I asked AI for specific apps targeting my needs and have purchased these through the app store. 

Web-based apps can become hard to locate and hard to cancel. It also shows profit before people. Yes, we know the app was in a study. So you now milk the public for it. There are better apps.

reviews.title: Frustrating at times
reviews.text: I can’t review the effectiveness of these brain games; I’ve only been doing them for a couple of weeks.  But some of the games  (Rythmn Recall!) are impossible with my iPad.  The problem isn’t my brain, it’s the iPad speaker and touch sensitivity.  Frustrating

reviews.title: Not fun
reviews.text: These games are more frustrating than fun. Actually not an ounce of fun. Might help my brain but will die of a heart attack from the high blood pressure these games cause.

reviews.title: Say what??
reviews.text: I used the free app daily for a few weeks and just deleted it. Poor graphics. Some games didn’t work. Inscrutable tracking— Stars, Moments (??) etc that don’t actually track your progress. The text that comes up post game moves so fast that you can’t read it, especially since the text doesn’t even fit the screen. Some of BrainHQ’s issues are pretty basic (such as fit-to-screen text). This seems like an early beta version.

reviews.title: Need to turn off blockers quickly
reviews.text: I use an application firewall that asks permission for incoming requests. If I don’t answer quickly enough, the app believes I’ve already used the free trial that day, so will not load. The option to always allow for this app will solve the problem. Either that or get really fast with hitting OK.

reviews.title: Good Training
reviews.text: I think this is probably pretty good. I did have one problem any time there is sound required. The audio breaks up so the instructions are not clear. It is this app because other apps I use with sound do not have this issue. The main issue I have is more personal in that having a rough time with an activity ruins the rest of my day and I feel truly stupid.

reviews.title: Frustrating and Unfulfilling
reviews.text: I’ve worked with Brain HQ for nearly a year now and I’m not willing to extend my subscription. The program continues to feed me the same exercises time after time and I don’t feel I’m progressing. I’ll try other options.

reviews.title: Don’t want my money?
reviews.text: Apparently the biggest brain challenge is the puzzle of how one would subscribe to unlock use beyond the free trial. Guys, you were just in the New York Times, you’d be printing money if you made it easy to pay.

reviews.title: Eyes
reviews.text: I have a v hard time seeing some of the prompts. That’s okay, I guess I need better glasses. However. I absolutely cannot read the quick notices tbat flash by when I finish a game. 10? 100? I have NO idea what is written. If it’s important enough to include then it’s important to slow it down. !!!!

reviews.title: doesn't show up in my subscriptions, but...
reviews.text: i've been trying to cancel the subscription.  it's not showing up under my subscriptions, but they still tried to charge me.  and considering i was passing for two of us, $155 is more than i'm willing to pay for an app that i got bored with

reviews.title: Inconsistent
reviews.text: Some of the games are good and once you to work harder to advance BUT some of the games are unclear and hard to figure out what to do.  In many of the games you have to start the game and figure out on your own what is going on by correct and incorrect answers.  There is one game where they say something about a person using their proper name but most of the names are ethnic names and unfortunately the spelling doesn’t match what the name sounds like or it is too hard to even understand what the name they are saying is.  Not a good test of memory if you can’t understand what they say or what the instructions are.  Could use some work.

reviews.title: Wrong orientation for me
reviews.text: Downloaded this because of news about benefits.  I can only hold my iPad in its vertical orientation.   For some reason this app only appears in landscape orientation and won’t rotate.  Not very brainy.

reviews.title: Great idea - Terrible app
reviews.text: The concept of the app is a great idea. The tests or games are probably quite helpful. But who knows!  No concrete metrics,scores over time, etc. Further, functionally, the app itself is mess. It is a mishmash of poor organization, obscure instructions, and lacks common elements to make the app usable. An example is that settings are nonexistent, even though it tells you to go to settings for some things, like managing your subscription. Another is that even to get to the subscription option, which I now regret doing, I had to hunt through a number of things.  Why isn’t that one of the options in the bars at the top? Most important, there is no apparent measurement that tells you how your scores or timing compare with expectations by age or any other criterion.  There are no scores, standards,  or measures that you can see for performance overtime. The strain of gold stars means nothing, except that the developers seem to think they are dealing with children under the age of five. The lack of information and feedback on your performance makes it somewhat useless. Doing the games is fine, but it is purely a pasttime.  Dealing with the app is an exercise in frustration. I have canceled my subscription.

reviews.title: Unhelpful setup
reviews.text: I was drawn to this after reading about a specific game that reduces the risk of Alzheimer’s. Unfortunately, it wants me to answer questions to guide me in another direction and won’t let me even access that game. Perhaps if I subscribe (and I’m locked in to a subscription) the app will, or maybe not. I don’t really have faith that it will. But it doesn’t really make me want to subscribe when it’s already burying the one thing that I want and making it impossible for me to even find.

reviews.title: Connect to internet???
reviews.text: Trying to sign up and keep getting a message that I must connect to the internet. I am on internet and also tried WiFi. Won’t let me sign up! Tried to online chat but all I get is a bot. Not jumping through hops to sign up, sorry. Moving on to another brain game.

reviews.title: Tried and tried
reviews.text: I twisted myself into such a pretzel to try to make an account for this app. No matter what I did, I couldn’t get into the app. Finally I realized that there were other brain training apps that probably don’t have this problem

reviews.title: Needs support for people with various colour blindness issues
reviews.text:
Update: I cancelled. I tried playing Hawk Eye on my iPad, the game where you spot the odd bird, and it’s literally impossible for me. I can barely see the birds, never mind the odd one out. They all blend into the tropical background. If I can even see the birds, even while staring at the screen in the training mode, what am I to do? This app is a good idea terribly executed. The whole idea is to test your brain, NOT your eyesight. 

I like this app, but sometimes fail due to issues with colour blindness. That is NOT the point of this app. Sometimes, when trying to distinguish between different butterflies, I can’t, not easily. That’s not because i’m stupid, or because the images disappear too fast, it’s literally my eyes. That should not be a determining factor. Please fix, or I’ll have to cancel.

reviews.title: Way Too Frustrating to Keep Going
reviews.text: At first this was a fun way to exercise my brain, but after a couple months I have started to hate it.  It gets way too hard way too fast.  Your reward for success is failure.  You have to fail twice for the difficulty to come down and then, once you succeed again, it goes right back up for more failure.  This is a poor design.  Once it is challenging, that is where it should stay so you can enjoy the exercises.  Forcing you to repeatedly go through the same exercise and fail over and over to get the stars you need to move on is frustrating, enraging and unproductive.  It takes longer and longer and gets ridiculous.  I can’t remember fifteen different train directions, nor can I remember fifteen different bits of gossip.  I have given up on this.  Whatever brain benefits it is giving me are far outweighed by the stress and frustration of the constant failure.  No thank you,

reviews.title: I am hating this now
reviews.text: At first I loved this and enjoyed it, but I have been using this app daily for about two months now and I am at a point now where it feels like torture.  Every morning it ramps up each exercise until I fail and then demands that I repeat and repeat it to get more stars and it just gets harder and takes longer to complete.  It should increase difficulty more gradually, not so obviously making you fail and then fail again and then as soon as you get one right, it gets immediately more difficult again and you fail again.  To be challenged is one thing.  To fail over and over is not helpful.  I can’t remember fifteen different train directions.  Succeeding at challenging puzzles is constructive and helpful and fun.  Repeatedly being pushed to failure is not.  It’s frustrating and I can’t keep doing it if I don’t enjoy it.

reviews.title: Very Boring
reviews.text: I am so disappointed in this app and wish I could get my money back. The exercises are very boring and the instructions are confusing as well.

reviews.title: Auditory Ace
reviews.text: This challenge does not display the card in time to select an answer.

reviews.title: One annoying thing
reviews.text: I appreciate that there’s a free version of this, but I find it really irritating that the stars at the end flash by so quickly that you can’t even read them!  Please slow it down a little.

reviews.title: Not user friendly
reviews.text:
It doesn’t make the simple stuff simple.  
Stars are awarded based on your performance as compared to others’ scores, not to an absolute. Progress bar is arbitrary, it moves back and forth with no consistency.  Bar doesn’t show you how far you are in the  test, you could go on for an hour and never  know how close you are to finishing. Directions are confusing as are the All Exercises listings.
